input.question:
A 61-year-old patient presented with cough, generalized musculoskeletal pain, and fever. The initial chest radiograph showed fine reticulonodular opacities throughout both lungs. Based on Figure 1, which statement is most accurate regarding the findings on the chest X-ray?

A) The reticulonodular opacities are predominantly located in the upper lobes and are symmetrical.

B) The reticulonodular opacities are predominantly located in the lower lobes and are asymmetrical.

C) The reticulonodular opacities are diffusely distributed throughout both lungs without a specific lobar predominance.

D) The reticulonodular opacities are associated with noticeable pleural effusion in the right lung.

E) The reticulonodular opacities are associated with noticeable pleural effusion in the left lung.

F) The reticulonodular opacities are accompanied by a significant shift of the mediastinum.

terminal.raw_response:
Answer: C) The reticulonodular opacities are diffusely distributed throughout both lungs without a specific lobar predominance.

Reason: Figure 1 shows fine reticulonodular opacities that involve both lungs symmetrically and extend from the apices to the bases, without clear upper- or lower-lobe predominance. There is no visible pleural effusion or mediastinal shift.

Choose the smallest applicable action set. Use ONLY these action kind strings: ground (localize-and-inspect), anatomy (anatomical reference), expert (focused expert observation), roi (manual original-pixel crop), paired (paired-image comparison). Natural-language descriptions and tool names are not action kind values. An action must address a stated option difference. Use actual image modality and view. A proposed diagnosis is a hypothesis, not an observation. Never apply a CXR-only tool to CT, lateral-only/montage grounding, or unconfirmed CXR. Grounding requires a frontal CXR. LLaVA-Med may describe other medical images. A classifier score cannot measure side, size, multiplicity or change. Segmentation supplies 14 anatomical regions, not lesion masks. For paired comparison identify the same object and only times explicitly stated in the question. If no available action addresses relevant uncertainty, return no actions and a reason; confidence alone is not a reason. Do not choose extra actions just to fill a budget.

Patient right is not display right. Any manual ROI uses stored display-pixel coordinates normalized [left,top,right,bottom], no flips. A patient-sided ROI requires a visibly read R/L marker and its normalized box; if unsure use bilateral/midline/full views. The controller converts grounding coordinates to original pixels; do not supply or reinterpret a grounding box by presumed patient side.
